quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #3
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: When driving on major highways, what should you do?

options.text: Be ready to react to road hazards.

questions.explanation: Stay alert on highways and be ready to react to unexpected hazards. Keep your eyes moving and do not stare at one spot for more than a few seconds. This helps prevent highway hypnosis.

questions.question: If you pass your exit on the interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.
Continue driving and use the next exit.
Put your vehicle in reverse to go back to the exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Do not make a last-minute turn into an exit. If you pass your exit, continue to the next one.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing, what should you do?
questions.explanation: When you see signs for a railroad crossing, slow down and look for a train. Be ready to stop. If red warning lights are flashing or the gate is down, stop 15 to 50 feet before the tracks. Do not try to go around the gate.

questions.question: How can stress affect your driving?

options.text: It reduces your ability to focus on driving.
It decreases your chances of an accident.
It causes you to fall asleep at the wheel.
It makes you more aware of others around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It reduces your ability to focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions can affect how well you drive. Worry, excitement, fear, anger, or sadness can reduce your concentration. If you feel emotionally unstable, it is better to wait before driving.

questions.question: Drinking alcohol and driving is:

options.text: Safe if you have only had a few drinks.
Only dangerous to the driver who drinks.

questions.explanation: Driving while impaired or intoxicated is a serious safety problem. Safe driving is not possible when you drink alcohol or take other drugs. Driving under the influence is dangerous to you and to others on the road.

questions.question: Why is night driving more difficult than day driving?

options.text: Cars overheat more quickly at night.
Visibility is reduced in the dark.
It is more likely to be raining at night.
You are more likely to encounter a motorcycle at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Visibility is reduced in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far. Use appropriate headlights and drive slowly enough to stop within the distance you can see ahead.

questions.question: What is the purpose of highway markings?

options.text: They are only found in construction zones.
They are usually red and blue in color.

questions.explanation: Highway markings provide important information for drivers. They help you position your vehicle correctly, show safe passing zones, and warn you about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Should motorists maintain a safe distance when driving near a cyclist?
questions.explanation: Drivers must be careful when near cyclists and keep a safe distance between their vehicle and the cyclist.

questions.question: You are entering a crowded freeway. What should you do to merge into traffic?

options.text: Use your side and rearview mirrors and check your blind spots.
Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of freeway traffic.
Yield to traffic already on the freeway.

questions.explanation: Use the entrance ramp to accelerate to the speed of freeway traffic. Yield to traffic already on the freeway. Check your mirrors and blind spots before merging to make sure you have room to safely enter.

questions.question: How can alcoholic beverages affect you?

options.text: It gives you a feeling of false confidence.

questions.explanation: Alcohol affects the parts of your brain that control judgment and self-control. It slows your reaction time, coordination, and balance. It also harms your vision and your ability to judge distance, making it hard to react to what is happening around you.

questions.question: Smoking and preparing to smoke while driving:
questions.explanation: Smoking while driving is a dangerous distraction. It takes your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road.

questions.question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the directions given by the flagger.
Do what other drivers are doing, even if it ignores the flagger's directions.
Assume the flagger should not be directing traffic.
Follow the normal traffic laws as if the area is not under construction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the flagger.
questions.explanation: You must slow down and follow directions from flaggers, signs, or police officers in construction zones. Not doing this is illegal and dangerous to workers.

questions.question: When approaching a school bus that has stopped with its stop arm extended, drivers should:

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait to proceed.
Honk the horn before passing the bus on the left.
Continue driving when you think most children have exited the bus.
Pass the bus before its door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait to proceed.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop when a school bus displays its stop signal. Do not move until the stop arm is withdrawn.

questions.question: Traffic signs and pavement markings:

options.text: Must be followed only when there are other vehicles nearby.
Must be followed only when a police officer is present.

questions.explanation: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings control traffic flow and guide drivers safely. You must always obey them.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Parking spaces are reserved for people with disabled parking permits.
Traffic in the lane must turn in the direction of the arrow.
Lanes are reserved for buses and carpools with at least two people.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parking spaces are reserved for people with disabled parking permits.
questions.explanation: This sign marks parking spaces reserved for people with disabled parking permits.

questions.question: Highway hypnosis can happen when:

options.text: You stare at the road for long periods of time.
You get too much sleep the night before driving.
You drive on short expressway trips.

questions.correctAnswerText: You stare at the road for long periods of time.
questions.explanation: Highway hypnosis happens when you stare straight ahead without looking around. You stop paying attention, which can cause you to crash into vehicles ahead of you.

questions.question: Never drive a vehicle through, around, or under any railroad gate or barrier.
questions.explanation: Never drive through, around, or under railroad crossing gates or barriers. It is illegal and very dangerous.

questions.question: A person walking with a white cane or guide dog is likely to be:

options.text: A person involved with a traffic study.

questions.explanation: You must always give the right-of-way to a blind person using a white cane or guide dog.

questions.question: What is the only way to reduce your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: Wait for your body to process the alcohol over time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for your body to process the alcohol over time.
questions.explanation: Only time reduces your BAC. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers cannot lower your BAC or make you sober. They may help you stay awake, but they do not reduce alcohol's effects.

questions.question: Drivers may not park:
questions.explanation: You cannot park in front of mailboxes, in front of driveways, on bridges, or in tunnels.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that there is a sharp right turn ahead.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spots?

options.text: Turn your head and look over your shoulders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas around your vehicle that your mirrors cannot show. Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check them.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Cars in right lane must slow down.
Pass only in the right lane.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that two lanes of traffic moving in the same direction will soon become one lane.

questions.question: Cell phones can be a serious source of driver distractions.
questions.explanation: While driving, do not use cell phones, computers, or other distracting devices. Keep your full attention on the road. Only use your phone to report a crash or emergency.

questions.question: You may drive around or under a gate that is being lowered or raised at a railroad crossing:

options.text: As long as an approaching train is not too close.
If your vehicle can do so without damaging the gate.
If you first look carefully in both directions.

questions.explanation: Flashing red lights, lowered crossing gates, and bells at a railroad crossing mean you must stop completely. Do not cross the tracks until the lights and bells stop and the gates are fully raised. Never drive around or under a moving gate.

questions.question: Two solid white lines across a traffic lane mark a crosswalk. As a driver, you should know:

options.text: Motor vehicles have the right-of-way over pedestrians in crosswalks.
Pedestrians in crosswalks have the right-of-way.
No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
Pedestrians must stay out of the way of all traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians in crosswalks have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Crosswalk lines show pedestrians where to cross safely. You must always stop for pedestrians in a crosswalk.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, you should:

options.text: Stay calm and move out of the aggressive driver's way.
Flash your lights to show the aggressive driver they are wrong.
Make a driving action to get back at the aggressive driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and move out of the aggressive driver's way.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and get out of the way of an aggressive driver. Do not try to get even with them. This will only make the situation more dangerous.

questions.question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, you must:

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear an emergency vehicle siren, pull over to the curb or side of the road and stop.

questions.question: You are driving and hear a siren behind you. You should:

options.text: Pull over to the right and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle behind you, pull over safely to the right side of the road and stop. If you are in heavy traffic directly in front of the vehicle, move slowly until you can get out of the way.

questions.question: The most effective way to reduce your risk of injury or death in a traffic crash is to:

options.text: Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.
Limit your driving to 3:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m.

questions.explanation: Wearing your seat belt is the single best way to reduce your risk of death or injury while driving.

questions.question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, look in your rearview and side mirrors. Also look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Make sure no one is trying to pass you or is in your blind spot.

questions.question: Orange is the color used for signs in construction work zones.
questions.explanation: Most signs in work areas are orange and diamond-shaped. Some are rectangular. These signs are reflective so they are easier to see at night.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol, what helps ensure safe driving?

options.text: Ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.
Take a cold shower before driving.
Stop drinking one half hour before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.
questions.explanation: The best way to stay safe is to arrange a ride home with a sober friend. Coffee and cold showers do not reduce alcohol in your body. It takes about one hour for your body to eliminate one drink of alcohol.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that the road ahead has curves. Slow down and be ready to turn.

questions.question: You have a green light at an intersection. Pedestrians are crossing against the red. You should:

options.text: Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrians.
Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
Drive close to the pedestrians and frighten them so they'll think twice before crossing against a red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
questions.explanation: Always let pedestrians cross safely, even if you have a green light. Be careful around pedestrians at all times.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: The left lane is reserved for vehicles with a specific number of occupants.
Specific turning movements are allowed from specific lanes.
Drivers in both lanes are responsible for merging smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane is reserved for vehicles with a specific number of occupants.
questions.explanation: This sign marks a high occupancy vehicle (HOV) lane. HOV lanes are for buses and vehicles with a driver and one or more passengers, as shown on the sign.

questions.question: Your brake lights tell other drivers that you:
questions.explanation: Your brake lights tell other drivers that you are slowing down or stopping. Keep your brake lights working at all times.

questions.question: When approaching a disabled pedestrian using a guide dog, white cane, or other assistive device, a driver should yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: A pedestrian using a guide dog, white cane, wheelchair, or other assistive device has the right-of-way. They have the same rights as any other pedestrian.

questions.question: This sign warns drivers about:

options.text: An upcoming curve in the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: An upcoming curve in the road.
questions.explanation: This sign means the road ahead curves to the right.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow traffic light, you should:

options.text: Speed up to avoid a red light.
Continue driving, as you have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Check what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a red light is coming soon. Stop if you can, unless you are already in the intersection.
